free_tier.stated: "Try Our 3 Day Trial" on the newsgroup page, whose title reads "3 Day Free Trial, Sign up today!". The same page advertises "50% off your first month of Supernews - that's just $5.99 to get started", against a regular "$11.99/MO" on the home page.
free_tier.notes: The trial is 3 days with no byte counter: "We do not limit how much Usenet you can access. Unlimited means Unlimited."

per_object_cap.stated: No per-object cap is published. The unit of retrieval is a Usenet article, roughly 750 KB by convention.

retention.stated: "5+ years Binary and 13+ years text" in the page description; the body says "5+ years Binary and 13+ years text retention".
retention.notes: The 5+ years figure is binary retention; the vendor gives no exact day count on the pages read.

egress.terms: No traffic meter is published: unlimited access and unlimited speed during the trial, 30 SSL connections. The only published charge is the $5.99 first month that follows the trial.
egress.free_allowance: 3 days, unlimited volume, at the client's line speed

interface_detail: NNTP over SSL (30 connections). The schema has no nntp token, so the array says unknown.
tooling: any NNTP client; the vendor ships no downloader
chaining: Three days at line speed is the largest single burst available behind a card: on a 100 Mbps line it is 3.24 TB, which is three times the client's monthly target, so one trial could cover a month if the line is fast and the card exists.

limits.value: unlimited speed, capped only by the client's line; 30 SSL connections

binding_note: During the three days nothing in the vocabulary fails: there is no byte counter and no speed throttle. After the trial the $11.99/month plan is still unlimited, so the binding constraint at 1 TiB/month is the client's own line, not the provider.

identity_cost.detail: The signup page at /signup/ renders the validation text of a card form: "Please provide valid card number", "Please provide valid card expiration", "Please provide valid card cvv", plus name, address, city, state and ZIP, and the footer says "Payments by GoCardless". A payment method is therefore captured before the trial starts.

reliability_note: The trial converts to $11.99/month unless cancelled; no suspension or throttle report was read.
confidence_note: Trial length and the unlimited terms are quoted from the vendor's own page today; the card gate is quoted from the vendor's signup form validation strings. No trial was executed.

evidence.proved: Page title "3 Day Free Trial, Sign up today!"; body "Try Our 3 Day Trial"; "We do not limit how much Usenet you can access. Unlimited means Unlimited."
"Please provide valid card number", "Please provide valid card expiration", "Please provide valid card cvv" and "Payments by GoCardless" - a card is required at signup
Regular price "$11.99/MO", "Unlimited Speed & Access", "30 SSL Connections"

notes: Repeatability: no vendor sentence on trial repetition was found; /terms/ answered 404. The card gate plus GoCardless makes a second signup a second payment relationship in practice, which is stated as the mechanism and not as a vendor rule. Abandonment: if the newsgroup page stops advertising the 3-day trial, the record becomes paid-only.

extras.repeat_basis: no sentence located; card gate only
